prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (≤500 words)

The manifesto outlines a ten-year Green New Deal to reach net zero emissions by 2030 while reforming the economy, public services, and democracy.

Core Green New Deal investments (c. £100+ billion per year, plus a Universal Basic Income):
- Energy: Rapid scale-up of renewables (around 70% of electricity from wind by 2030, with solar, tidal, hydro, geothermal supplying most of the rest); grid expansion and storage; demand-side management; end subsidies for oil and gas; rising carbon tax on fossil fuels and imported embedded emissions; ban fracking; prohibit new nuclear; stronger interconnectors with Europe.
- Housing: Insulate every home by 2030; deep retrofit 1 million buildings per year; 10 million homes with rooftop renewables by 2030; replace gas boilers with heat pumps and district heat; at least 100,000 new social homes annually to Passivhaus standard; stronger building regs and rental energy standards; planning that reduces car dependence.
- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than driving; nationwide bus franchising and restored routes; electrify key rail lines and expand capacity; bring rail into public ownership over 10 years; £2.5bn/yr for walking/cycling infrastructure; end road-capacity expansion and new runways; frequent flyer levy and domestic aviation tax reforms; end sale of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030; national EV charging rollout; default 20mph in residential areas.
- Industry: R&D and standards to decarbonise processes; grants to replace high-carbon kit; training and apprenticeships (£2bn/yr); mutual regional banks; right to repair, 10‑year warranties on white goods; near-100% recycling infrastructure; ban most single-use plastics; extended producer responsibility; CCS for steel/cement.
- Food, farming & forestry: Shift subsidies to agroecology, organics, mixed farming and agroforestry; reduce pesticides and nitrogen use; plant 700m trees; restore hedgerows; protect soils and water; urban food growing; right to food; natural flood management; GM moratorium; phased tax on meat/dairy with revenues supporting farm transition; clear eco-labelling.

Incomes and welfare:
- Phase in a Universal Basic Income: adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week; supplements for disabled people, lone parents, and children; retain housing benefit where needed; integrate with a 35-hour free childcare offer from 9 months; replace most means-tested benefits and end sanctions.

Democracy and governance:
- Proportional representation for all elections; votes at 16; elected second chamber; state funding for parties; tighter media plurality rules and digital rights; citizens’ assemblies; Future Generations Act; new department led by a “Carbon Chancellor”; restructure security, migration, and arms-export functions; devolution and £10bn/yr uplift to councils plus £3bn/yr climate adaptation; free home care at home for over‑65s in England.

Public services:
- NHS: +£6bn/yr rising to 2030; restore nursing bursaries; roll back internal market; expand community and mental health; free contraception and PrEP.
- Education: +£4bn/yr; smaller classes; end high-stakes testing/Ofsted; formal schooling from age 6; arts restored; free higher education and debt write-off; expanded FE/adult learning; climate and nature curricula.

Rights, justice, environment, and animals:
- Stronger protections for nature (Clean Air Act, Environmental Protection Commission, right to roam, marine protections); comprehensive anti-discrimination measures; humane migration system; halve prison population via prevention and restorative justice; legal, regulated drug framework; animal sentience in law; ban hunting, live exports, cages; reduce and replace animal testing.

Tax and funding:
- Carbon tax (~£76.7bn/yr); consolidated income tax treating income from wealth like work; corporation tax to 24%; HMRC independence; anti-avoidance measures; abolish non‑dom status; long-term Land Value Tax replacing council tax/business rates (phased, revenue-neutral first decade, protections for low-income/asset‑rich).
- Small business support: regional mutual banks; 15% of public contracts to SMEs; faster payments; VAT cuts for hospitality/culture; higher Employment Allowance.
- End “wasteful spending”: cancel nuclear deterrent replacement, major road building, airport expansion, and HS2; reform Help to Buy/Right to Buy.
- Totals: ~£141.5bn/yr operational spend funded by tax changes and savings (~£124.4bn new revenue + ~£29.4bn savings); ~£94.4bn/yr capital via borrowing; expected private co‑investment ~£50bn/yr.
